label: copy-phase fed-back "1" input, strongest when the token being output is x (or 1/m/h)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and about 97% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is the digit 1 (a few weak activations on input x). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Only about 8.5% of copy-phase 1-inputs fire, so the selectivity depends on the output: activation is largest when the token being output right after the 1 is x (input 1 and output x alone gives precision 0.73 and 47% of mass; top examples are "... 1 x x ..."). Outputs 1, m and h also boost it. It is weak or absent at recall_idx <= 1 and peaks at recall_idx 3-4. More digits in the sequence raise the firing rate. The predicate (input 1, output in {x,1,m,h}, recall_idx >= 2) gets dev F1 about 0.51 and mass recall 0.73. The broad description (copy-phase input 1) covers 97% of mass but with low precision, so the remaining dependence on the output token is only partly captured.
